core.title: Keep DTOs pure immutable data
core.given: a DTO — the shape crossing a boundary — declared in a scanned source file assigned to a layer role (not a test role, not a never-scanned tree)
core.when: that DTO is declared, changed, or present in any scanned file (including pre-existing declarations)
core.then: the DTO MUST be pure immutable data: no behavior members, and every field immutable.
prefer: Keep DTOs as immutable data: immutable fields only, no behavior members.
Put behavior in the layer that consumes or produces the DTO.
During GREEN: add only the immutable data fields the current boundary behavior requires.
During GREEN: reuse existing functions for transformation or behavior when available; add a small standalone function only when the current acceptance needs it.
avoid: Attaching convenience operations (behavior members) to the DTO.
Making fields mutable to simplify implementation.
core.why: Behavior on a DTO means behaviour crossed the boundary too, coupling both sides to an implementation rather than data; a mutable field lets the receiver change what the sender said. Both look harmless in one file and become impossible to unpick once a second consumer exists.
evidence: The stack's convention check reports no behavior member or mutable field on any DTO declaration in scanned files.
The affected DTO remains pure immutable data (all fields immutable, no behavior members).
verification: The check inspects every DTO declaration in scanned source files and flags any behavior member and any field not marked immutable in the stack's idiom.
Files assigned to a test role and the profile's never-scanned trees are outside the check; the exact classification is owned by the stack's checker.
External-package references (recognized per the stack's external-import idiom) resolve outside the project graph and are not part of role assignment.
A file with no role assignment is outside the rule rather than in violation of it.
Severity 3; disposition strict: the check fails on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

fires: A coder adds or edits a DTO declaration in a source file assigned to a layer role.
A task adds a field to an existing DTO to carry data across a boundary.
A scanned source file assigned to a layer role already contains a DTO with a behavior member or a mutable field, even if the current change did not touch it.
The convention check reports a behavior member or a mutable field on any DTO declaration.
doesNotFire: The DTO declaration lives in a test role or in a never-scanned tree.
The file carries no layer role.
The scanned files contain no DTO declaration at all.

profileRequirements.meaning: How the stack declares and recognizes a DTO, the data shape crossing a boundary: the declaring construct and its naming pattern.

profileRequirements.meaning: What pure immutable data means for a DTO in the stack: which member kinds count as behavior, and how field immutability is expressed.

neutralityNotes: The TypeScript terms 'method member' and 'readonly' have no stack-neutral equivalent, so the obligation is stated as 'no behavior members, every field immutable' and its concrete meaning is delegated to the proposed keys idiom.dto_shape#dto_declaration and idiom.dto_shape#dto_purity (also listed in profileRequirements). 'During GREEN' is an ATDD phase term and was kept. Per-rule severity (3) and the strict disposition stay in core verification. The Bun detector's textual member-splitting mechanics and its detector/finding ids remain bunOnly. roots.excluded is restricted to the one stack-wide list of vendored/generated trees ('vendored/build directories'); the test-file exclusion is carried through roles.assignment and its test-role classification, and the core keeps the Bun text's deference of the exact never-scanned classification to the stack's checker.
